ei.title: In line with this, like many expressions and communications,...
ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: In line with this, like many expressions and communications, emotion is expressed in the face, voice, and body and redundantly even within each mode. Faces cannot be discounted as carriers of emotion. ( ) Tennis matches require forceful actions of the body and are played to a crowd, so the dominance of the body over the face is natural. ( ) Tennis matches are only one of a vast range of situations that cause emotion. ( ) Many encounters, both intense and casual, involve people sitting or standing face-to-face, where emotion is carried primarily by the face and voice and less by the rest of the body. ( ) Human communication is typically redundant, presumably at least in part to reduce error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. ( ) People who are blind can grasp emotion from voice, both prosody and words; people who are deaf can grasp emotion from face and body.

questions.passage: In line with this, like many expressions and communications, emotion is (A)[expressed / suppressed] in the face, voice, and body and redundantly even within each mode. Faces cannot be discounted as carriers of emotion. ( ) Tennis matches require forceful actions of the body and are played to a crowd, so the (B)[dominance / submission] of the body over the face is natural. ( ) Tennis matches are only one of a vast range of situations that cause emotion. ( ) Many encounters, both intense and casual, involve people sitting or standing face-to-face, where emotion is carried primarily by the face and voice and less by the rest of the body. ( ) Human communication is typically (C)[redundant / unique], presumably at least in part to reduce error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. ( ) People who are blind can grasp emotion from voice, both prosody and words; people who are deaf can grasp emotion from face and body.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① expressed — dominance — redundant ←정답

② suppressed — dominance — redundant: (A)에 suppressed(억압된)는 부적절. 본문은 감정이 얼굴, 목소리, 몸으로 '표현된다(expressed)'고 함.

③ expressed — submission — redundant: (B)에 submission(복종)은 부적절. 테니스 경기에서 얼굴보다 몸의 '지배력(dominance)'이 자연스럽다는 맥락.

④ expressed — dominance — unique: (C)에 unique(독특한)는 부적절. 인간 소통은 전형적으로 '중복적(redundant)'이라는 맥락.

questions.passage: In line with this, like many expressions and communications, emotion is expressed in the face, voice, and body and redundantly even within each mode. Faces cannot be (A)[discounted / celebrated] as carriers of emotion. ( ) Tennis matches require forceful actions of the body and are played to a crowd, so the dominance of the body over the face is natural. ( ) Tennis matches are only one of a vast range of situations that cause emotion. ( ) Many encounters, both (B)[intense / trivial] and casual, involve people sitting or standing face-to-face, where emotion is carried primarily by the face and voice and less by the rest of the body. ( ) Human communication is typically redundant, presumably at least in part to (C)[reduce / amplify] error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. ( ) People who are blind can grasp emotion from voice, both prosody and words; people who are deaf can grasp emotion from face and body.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
④ discounted — intense — reduce ←정답

① celebrated — intense — reduce: (A)에 celebrated(칭송받는)는 부적절. 얼굴이 감정 전달자로 '무시될 수 없다(cannot be discounted)'는 맥락.

② discounted — trivial — reduce: (B)에 trivial(사소한)은 부적절. 본문은 '강렬하고(intense) 일상적인' 만남을 언급.

③ discounted — intense — amplify: (C)에 amplify(증폭하다)는 부적절. 본문은 오류를 '줄이기(reduce)' 위해 중복 소통한다고 함.

questions.passage: In line with this, like many expressions and communications, emotion is expressed in the face, voice, and body and redundantly even within each mode. Faces cannot be discounted as (A)[carriers / obstacles] of emotion. ( ) Tennis matches require forceful actions of the body and are played to a crowd, so the dominance of the body over the face is natural. ( ) Tennis matches are only one of a vast range of situations that cause emotion. ( ) Many encounters, both intense and casual, involve people sitting or standing face-to-face, where emotion is carried (B)[primarily / marginally] by the face and voice and less by the rest of the body. ( ) Human communication is typically redundant, (C)[presumably / certainly] at least in part to reduce error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. ( ) People who are blind can grasp emotion from voice, both prosody and words; people who are deaf can grasp emotion from face and body.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
④ carriers — primarily — presumably ←정답

① carriers — marginally — presumably: (B)에 marginally(미미하게)는 부적절. 감정이 '주로(primarily)' 얼굴과 목소리로 전달된다는 맥락.

② obstacles — primarily — presumably: (A)에 obstacles(장애물)는 부적절. 얼굴은 감정의 '전달자(carriers)'로서 무시될 수 없다는 맥락.

③ carriers — primarily — certainly: (C)에 certainly(확실히)는 문맥상 가능하나, 본문은 '아마도(presumably)' 오류를 줄이기 위해서라고 추측 표현을 사용.

questions.passage: In line with this, like many expressions and communications, emotion is ①<u>expressed</u> in the face, voice, and body and redundantly even within each mode. Faces cannot be discounted as ②<u>carriers</u> of emotion. ( ) Tennis matches require forceful actions of the body and are played to a crowd, so the dominance of the body over the face is ③<u>artificial</u>. ( ) Tennis matches are only one of a vast range of situations that cause emotion. ( ) Many encounters, both intense and casual, involve people sitting or standing face-to-face, where emotion is carried primarily by the face and voice and less by the rest of the body. ( ) Human communication is typically ④<u>redundant</u>, presumably at least in part to reduce error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. ( ) People who are blind can grasp emotion from voice, both prosody and words; people who are deaf can grasp emotion from face and body.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① expressed(표현된): 감정이 얼굴, 목소리, 몸으로 '표현된다'는 맥락에 적절.

② carriers(전달자): 얼굴이 감정의 '전달자'로 무시될 수 없다는 맥락에 적절.

③ artificial(인위적인) ←정답: 테니스에서 몸이 얼굴보다 우세한 것은 '자연스러운(natural)' 것이라는 맥락. artificial은 반의어로 부적절.

④ redundant(중복적인): 인간 소통이 전형적으로 '중복적'이라는 맥락에 적절.

questions.passage: In line with this, like many expressions and communications, emotion is expressed in the face, voice, and body and redundantly even within each mode. Faces cannot be discounted as carriers of emotion. ( ) Tennis matches require ①<u>forceful</u> actions of the body and are played to a crowd, so the dominance of the body over the face is natural. ( ) Tennis matches are only one of a ②<u>narrow</u> range of situations that cause emotion. ( ) Many encounters, both intense and ③<u>casual</u>, involve people sitting or standing face-to-face, where emotion is carried primarily by the face and voice and less by the rest of the body. ( ) Human communication is typically redundant, presumably at least in part to reduce error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. ( ) People who are blind can ④<u>grasp</u> emotion from voice, both prosody and words; people who are deaf can grasp emotion from face and body.

det.analysis:
① forceful(강력한): 테니스 경기가 몸의 '강력한' 동작을 필요로 한다는 맥락에 적절.

② narrow(좁은) ←정답: 본문은 테니스가 감정을 유발하는 '방대한(vast)' 범위의 상황 중 하나라고 함. narrow는 반의어로 부적절.

③ casual(일상적인): '강렬하고 일상적인(intense and casual)' 만남이라는 맥락에 적절.

④ grasp(파악하다): 시각장애인이 목소리에서 감정을 '파악할' 수 있다는 맥락에 적절.

( ) Human communication is typically redundant, presumably at least in part to ④<u>increase</u> error; if you miss part of a message, say, in a noisy restaurant, you might get another part, enough to understand. det.analysis:
① redundantly(중복적으로): 감정이 각 방식 내에서도 '중복적으로' 표현된다는 맥락에 적절.

② dominance(지배): 테니스에서 얼굴보다 몸의 '지배력'이 자연스럽다는 맥락에 적절.

③ primarily(주로): 감정이 '주로' 얼굴과 목소리로 전달된다는 맥락에 적절.

④ increase(증가시키다) ←정답: 본문은 소통의 중복성이 오류를 '줄이기(reduce)' 위함이라고 함. increase는 반의어로 부적절.
